question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's entrenched position within the Chinese Communist Party drives trader consensus that he will remain in power through the end of 2026. Recent developments, including his active diplomatic engagements, appointments of loyal officials to key training and disciplinary roles, and preparations for the 21st Party Congress in 2027, signal continued consolidation of authority rather than any transition. No public signals of resignation, elite challenges, or health concerns have emerged, while ongoing purges reinforce control over the military and state apparatus. This stability aligns with the implied probability exceeding 95 percent for "No." Rare scenarios that could still shift outcomes include an abrupt health crisis, severe economic disruption prompting coordinated internal opposition, or unforeseen leadership maneuvers ahead of the congress.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 2028 Democratic presidential nomination remains tightly contested in prediction markets because no major contender has launched a campaign more than two years before the primaries, leaving traders to weigh governors, senators, and House members with distinct profiles and regional bases. Gavin Newsom holds the narrow lead at 18.3% amid his visibility as California governor, yet his earlier market share has eroded. Jon Ossoff has climbed to 16.2% on recent polling inclusion and Senate profile, while Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez sits at 15.0% supported by progressive networks. Kamala Harris and others trail further back. Upcoming 2026 midterms, early primary-state polling, and any formal announcements could widen gaps by clarifying electability signals and coalition strength among the broad field.
